clue.text: Relatives providing sutherland with a wig during broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered far and wide, so the letters of these words are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A family tells of Sutherland being fitted with a wig during a radio or television broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' signals the anagram of SUTHERLAND, A and WIG together; 'providing' and 'during' only join the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A spouse's female children's partners, or a son's wife, are relations acquired by marriage, so in-laws count as relatives.

clue.text: Worried parent around western harbour

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the abbreviation, holding it inside them
worried suggests being upset or disturbed, so the letters of parent are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: An anxious mother or father circles a harbour in the west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worried' turns PARENT into ANTERP, and 'around' puts that round W, giving ANT-W-ERP.
explanation.definitionFit: Antwerp in Belgium is one of Europe's largest seaports, so the city serves as an example of a harbour.

clue.text: Loads of tricks

parts.note: reads as a lot of pranks or magic, but in bridge it is the contract to take every one of the thirteen tricks

explanation.walkthrough: Tricks here are the card-game sense, not jokes; 'Loads' hints at both the sheer number and at 'grand' meaning a thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, winning all thirteen tricks in a deal is the highest possible contract, so it is the most tricks one can take.

clue.text: This artist has strangely portrayed tahitians

indicators.note: strangely portrayed means the letters of the artist plus has are shown in an odd order, spelling tahitians

explanation.surface: A painter is said to have depicted islanders of Tahiti in an unusual style.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the artist's name together with HAS, rearranged, gives TAHITIANS; take H, A, S out of TAHITIANS and the six letters left make the painter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian Renaissance master Tiziano Vecellio is the painter in question, so he is the artist meant.

clue.text: Start to throw teargas around race-meetings

indicators.note: around here means turned about, so the letters are moved round into a different order
the start of a word is its opening letter, so the first letter of throw is taken

explanation.surface: Someone begins hurling tear gas at a series of boat-race events.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start to' takes T from 'throw'; 'around' then shuffles T with TEARGAS to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Regattas are meetings at which boat races are held, so they are race-meetings on water.

clue.text: One young man takes in one long story

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: takes in means the young man swallows the second piece, holding it inside

parts.note: a lad is a young man or boy
again the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A single youth welcomes someone into a lengthy tale.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces run I, then LAD with I placed in it: I + L(I)AD.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic poem about the siege of Troy is a famously long narrative, so it is a long story.

clue.text: Discarded felt?

parts.note: the answer read as wordplay says the letters of the first word, set off (out of order), give this clue word

explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as an instruction, the first word with 'off' as an anagram signal, and it yields 'felt'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something omitted from a list or dropped from a team has been put aside, so it was thrown out or discarded.

clue.text: Playing one takes your breath away

definitions.text: Playing one takes your breath away

parts.words: Playing one takes your breath away
parts.note: reads as something astonishing, but literally describes an instrument blown with the lungs, such as a flute or trumpet

explanation.walkthrough: 'takes your breath away' usually means amazes; here it is literal, since the instrument is sounded by blowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Flutes, clarinets and trumpets are sounded by blowing into them, so playing one uses up the player's breath.

clue.text: Instructor once resorted to a copy

indicators.note: resorted is read as re-sorted, sorted again, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A teacher, once again, turned to a duplicate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resorted' looks like 'turned to' but is read as 're-sorted', signalling the anagram of INSTRUCTOR and ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuilt model or a re-enactment of an event imitates the original, so it is a kind of copy.

clue.text: Take out short passage from a book

definitions.meaning: to remove or pull out, as with a tooth
a quoted excerpt or selection from a longer written work

explanation.surface: Remove a brief excerpt from a volume.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to remove or draw out; as a noun it means an excerpt quoted from a text.

clue.text: Good bit of music when with working dog

parts.note: a riff is a short repeated phrase in popular music
on means working or switched on, as a machine is

explanation.surface: A good tune strikes up while a sheepdog or similar working animal is around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working dog' looks like one phrase, but 'working' gives ON and 'dog' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The griffon is a breed of small wiry-coated terrier-like hound, so it is a type of dog.

clue.text: Arrangement with bank about plan

parts.note: over can mean about or concerning, as in a quarrel over money
a draft is a preliminary plan or outline

explanation.surface: A deal with the bank concerning a scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: An agreed facility to spend beyond one's balance is arranged with the bank, which is why the long phrase is a fair definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank agrees in advance to let a customer withdraw more than is in the account, so the facility is an arrangement with the lender.

clue.text: Girl carries stolen article of clothing

indicators.note: carries means the name holds the next piece inside it, as if carrying it

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name, from Diana
hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: A young woman makes off with a pilfered garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carries' signals the container. The garment is the loincloth worn by many men in India, a word solvers outside South Asia may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: The loincloth wrapped around the waist by many Hindu men is a traditional garment, so it is an article of clothing.

clue.text: Provide in a compliant manner

definitions.meaning: to furnish or give what is needed
the adverb from supple, meaning pliantly or yieldingly

explanation.surface: Give what is asked, obligingly.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the rare adverb of 'supple', pronounced with a short final syllable, meaning flexibly.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to furnish or give; as an adverb formed from supple it means pliantly, yieldingly.

clue.text: Mum's pets? Big dogs

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mum, and the 's is kept
a pet is a fit of sulking, as is a tiff, a petty quarrel

explanation.surface: Are these mother's favourite animals? They are large hounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pets' looks like animals, chiming with the dogs, but is the old sense of a sulk or huff, like a tiff.
explanation.definitionFit: The mastiff is a massive, heavy-boned guard breed, so mastiffs are large dogs.

clue.text: Happen to give off vapour

definitions.meaning: to exhale moisture, as a plant does through its leaves

explanation.surface: Come to emit steam.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to occur or come to pass, and in biology it means to release water vapour through pores.

clue.text: Man cores fruit — like a picnic?

parts.note: Alf is a man's name, short for Alfred

indicators.note: fruit is used loosely as a mixing signal, the letters of cores being tossed like a fruit salad into a new order

explanation.surface: A man removes the cores from some fruit, perhaps for an outdoor meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fruit' looks like the thing being cored, but it is an unusual anagram signal, perhaps as letters tossed like a fruit salad; 'like a picnic' asks for an adjective phrase meaning outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A picnic is eaten in the open air, so it is an outdoor affair, which is what the Italian-derived phrase means.

clue.text: Like to put back together, but wanting a second

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the pieces named next are missing from the longer word

parts.note: to reassemble is to put something back together
a gives A and S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: Someone would like to rebuild something, but is short of a second.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove A and S (second) from REASSEMBLE. 'Like' is a verb here: to look like.
explanation.definitionFit: To be similar to or take after someone is to look like them, so the verb sense of like matches.

clue.text: Run around small person in a tent

parts.note: a camper sleeps in a tent

explanation.surface: Dash about near a little man sleeping under canvas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' belongs to the definition 'Run around', not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To scurry about playfully, as children or small animals do, is to dash around.

clue.text: Of course it's expensive stuff that can make endless avarice

indicators.note: can make means the remaining letters can be rearranged to form something new
endless means the word avarice loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Naturally, a costly delicacy is bound to stir up greed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the E from AVARICE, leaving AVARIC, and 'can make' rearranges those six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sturgeon roe is a famously costly luxury food, so it is expensive stuff.

clue.text: They're tickled when you play the piano

definitions.text: They're tickled when you play the piano

parts.words: They're tickled when you play the piano
parts.note: playing the piano is jokingly called tickling the keys, which were once made of elephant tusk

explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'tickle the ivories' means to play the piano.
explanation.definitionFit: Piano keys were traditionally faced with tusk material, and the slang phrase for playing is tickling them.

clue.text: After last letter I send snappy answer

indicators.note: the last letter of the word after is taken, its final letter

parts.note: to post a letter is to send it

explanation.surface: Having finished the final letter of a reply, I mail a quick-witted response.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last letter' looks like Z or a letter in the post, but means the final letter of 'After', R. The answer is a variant spelling of riposte.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick, sharp retort, so it is a snappy answer.

clue.text: Expert's fracture

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means first-rate or expert, as in a ... shot
a break or split in something

explanation.surface: A skilled person's broken bone.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means highly skilled, as in a crack shot; as a noun it means a break or split.

clue.text: This is a vessel put up for sauce

indicators.note: put here means this word with up put after it would be the sauce, so taking up away from the sauce leaves the vessel

parts.note: ketchup is a tomato sauce
taken as written

explanation.surface: This boat is raised to fetch the gravy.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'this, with UP put after it, stands for sauce': KETCHUP less UP leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A ketch is a two-masted sailing boat, so it is a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Sudden inspiration doesn't start in bad weather

indicators.note: doesn't start means the word for the idea loses its opening letter

parts.note: a brainstorm is a sudden clever idea

explanation.surface: A flash of genius fails to get going during a downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the first letter, B, from BRAINSTORM leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy downpour accompanied by wind is a spell of foul conditions, so it is bad weather.

clue.text: I'm upset about charges

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: I am distressed by the accusations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder; 'about' rearranges IMUPSET.
explanation.definitionFit: To impute a fault is to attribute it to someone, so the verb means accuses, or charges.

clue.text: Head takes in good view

indicators.note: takes in means the head swallows the next piece, holding it inside

parts.note: onion is old slang for the head, as in use your onion
pi, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for good

explanation.surface: The headteacher accepts a sound point of view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes in' signals the container. Onion is old British slang for the head ('use your onion' means think), and PI for good is a crossword convention from pious.
explanation.definitionFit: A view held on a subject is a belief or judgement, which is the same as one's opinion.

clue.text: In full, the point of sinner's heart

definitions.text: In full, the point of sinner's heart

parts.words: In full, the point of sinner's heart
parts.note: the middle three letters of sinner's are N, N, E, a compass abbreviation; written out in full, it names a direction between due north and northeast

explanation.surface: Spelt out at length, the essential message of a wrongdoer's soul.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of SINNERS (seven letters) is its central three, NNE, the compass point abbreviation; 'In full' asks for it written out.
explanation.definitionFit: On a sixteen-point compass rose, the bearing midway between due north and northeast is this direction.
